system.boundary: Build an eight-module series battery pack with coupled electrical storage, distributed module thermal states, and an actively regulated liquid-cooling path.
engineering_objects: P9-XBATT01 plant and controller described by the current public task contract
Measured output interfaces: battery_state, thermal_state, cooling_state, thermal_flux
physical_paths: Pack current must flow through the module electrical states, module losses must heat the corresponding thermal states, and the cooling actuator must remove heat through the coolant path rather than by directly overwriting temperatures.
functional_paths: Build an eight-module series battery pack with coupled electrical storage, distributed module thermal states, and an actively regulated liquid-cooling path.

Across the declared range and a repeatable multi-level discharge profile around discharge_current, regulate cooling to keep every module below 318 K, limit module temperature spread to 3 K, maintain module voltage above 36 V and SOC above 0.15, and respond to the temporary flow degradation without violating charge or thermal causality.
The cooling-control and warning strategies are not prescribed.
information_paths: ambient_temperature, initial_soc, discharge_current, module_parameter_spread, cooling_fault_fraction, cooling_fault_time -> P9-XBATT01 plant/control path -> battery_state, thermal_state, cooling_state, thermal_flux
modes_and_events: Read ambient_temperature, initial_soc, discharge_current, module_parameter_spread, cooling_fault_fraction, and cooling_fault_time from base-workspace variables.
cooling_fault_fraction is the severity of a 30 s cooling-flow degradation beginning at cooling_fault_time;
The detailed pump/fault characteristic may be nonlinear.

feedback_and_control_causality: Build an eight-module series battery pack with coupled electrical storage, distributed module thermal states, and an actively regulated liquid-cooling path.

Pack current must flow through the module electrical states, module losses must heat the corresponding thermal states, and the cooling actuator must remove heat through the coolant path rather than by directly overwriting temperatures.
The cooling actuator has a normalized command, a rated delivered mass flow of 0.30 kg/s, a rated loop pressure drop of 100 kPa, and rated electrical auxiliary power of 120 W at full command;
